comments.author: @pixelsort
comments.text: Thinking about this for the first time, it seems that in the challenge of summarization, a document would be composed of meaningful ideas that incur penalties to various scorable attributes depending primarily upon the concision required to finish the summary beneath some word or sentence limit. But, the degradation of those properties would not be linear. And the variability would occur in somewhat unpredictable ways depending upon the words available to the target language, average contextual word density within the target language, restrictions on tone and style, and so on. Since all of this is relatively obvious to me, I'd imagine that what Altman really means is that he has the LLMs playing the telephone game through a descent of maximum output length and some sort of quorum/consesus mechanism that does the quality control.

comments.author: @alexanderbrown-dg3sy
comments.text:
No. From someone who actually knows what they’re talking about. OpenAI’s gpt2 chatbot, I believe did something I was tweaking about months ago. Why I stop tweeting. Self-reinforcement improvement is said to have a 3 iteration saturation point. I said this dumb and experts aren’t experts 😂. Based on alphacode2 benchmarks, the solution was clear just compute intensive. Extended test-time compute per prompt, millions, either use LM as a judge or better yet use Listwise preference optimization across that entire output corpus, since LM are  partial markov processes…basically, vastly decreasing that probabilistic space during inference this way can vastly improve performance.

Fyi you can now do the same with llama3-70b. Expensive though.

comments.text: Every time you talk about EA, it's super cringe. EA is not, and has never been, an organization. EA is a philosophy. He's been publishing and ringing alarm bells on this topic for literal decades. The only organization he's had influence on was MIRI, which isn't meaningfully in the EA camp. So why is he being brought up as if he's a major player in the movement?
